evidence: Clear module-based structure with well-defined packages (e.g., fuzzers, monitors, restarters, mutants, connections, loggers) that encapsulate related functionality
Consistent use of interface-based abstraction (e.g., IFuzzer, IMonitor, IRestarter, ITargetConnection, IMutant) with concrete implementations inside modules
Heavy intra-module dependencies within the same package hierarchy; low inter-package coupling (avg_fan_out=2.85, max depth=4)
Shared core modules (e.g., primitives, blocks, mutants, graph, session) are composed together at runtime rather than deployed separately
No evidence of network-transparent service boundaries, deployment isolation, or independent versioning (rules out microservices_like)
No strict separation of presentation/business/persistence layers (rules out layered)
Main entry point in __main__.py orchestrates modules rather than routing through adapters (rules out hexagonal)
No clear model-view-controller separation in core architecture (rules out mvc)
Not script-based as it has strong object-oriented structure, abstractions, and modularity beyond procedural scripts
risks: Tight coupling between modules (e.g., session depends directly on many components) may hinder independent testing or replacement
Monolithic deployment may limit scalability or operational flexibility for large deployments
Missing service boundaries could complicate horizontal scaling or distributed deployments
